If sentiment is positive in the last 3 days and forecast is trending up, reduce forecast by 2–5% in late horizon to avoid over-optimism.  
If sentiment is negative and forecast is trending down, increase forecast by 2–5% in mid horizon to counteract pessimism.  
If sentiment is neutral and forecast diverges sharply from recent history, apply a 3–7% correction toward historical mean in early horizon.  
When sentiment swings from positive to negative within 5 days, reduce forecast slope by 15–30% in mid horizon to reflect sentiment reversal.  
If sentiment is consistently positive over 10+ days and forecast is flat, increase forecast by 3–8% in late horizon to capture momentum.  
If sentiment is consistently negative over 10+ days and forecast is flat, decrease forecast by 3–8% in late horizon to reflect bearish sentiment.
